newsitem.title: USA: Aliyev confirms four oil deals to be signed.
newsitem.headline: Aliyev confirms four oil deals to be signed.

text.p: Azeri President Haydar Aliyev on Thursday confirmed that four U.S. companies are expected to sign oil development contracts with the Azerbaijan state oil company SOCAR on Friday.
He said agreements worth a total of $8 billion in new investments would be signed with units of Chevron, Mobil, Exxon, and Amoco.
Earlier oil production agreements with U.S. and other companies were worth a total of $30 billion in investment, he told U.S. business executives here.
He said along with rich oil reserves, Azerbaijan had abundant natural gas reserves. "We will be able to produce a lot of natural gas in Azerbaijan," he said.
Following a memorandum signed last year, Exxon is negotiating terms to develop a deepwater natural gas field in the Caspian, which Aliyev said Exxon officials called "very, very rich" in gas.
Azerbaijan plans to begin exporting oil this year from the Caspian Sea fields being developed by the AIOC consortium, led by British Petroleum and Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap (Statoil).
"I believe the pipeline will be ready this year, very soon, and we will be able to export the early oil," he said, referring to a pipeline through Russia to the Black Sea port of Novorossisk.
He said a second pipeline to Georgia's outlet of Supsa is expected to be ready by October 1998, to carry more early oil from Azerbaijan and Chevron's production from the Tengiz field in Kazakhstan.
Plans for the main export pipeline for Azerbaijan's Caspian production are still being debated. "I hope that very soon we will have some discussions," Aliyev said. "Maybe we will announce a tender."

He reiterated that he wanted the pipeline route to go from the Azeri capital Baku to the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan. Alternative options would route the big pipeline to Supsa or to Novorossisk.
